new_entities.name: Ropinirole for restless legs syndrome
new_entities.description: Use of ropinirole to reduce symptom burden in adults with restless legs syndrome.

new_entities.name: Disease severity
new_entities.description: Overall severity of a disorder, often measured by validated symptom scales such as the International Restless Legs Scale.

edges.effect_quant: Across multiple randomized trials, ropinirole lowers International Restless Legs Scale scores versus placebo. In a 381-patient US trial the adjusted treatment difference at 12 weeks was -3.7 points, in TREAT RLS 2 the difference was -2.5 points, and in very symptomatic patients with baseline IRLS at least 24 the placebo-adjusted effect remained -2.5 points at 26 weeks.
edges.population: adults with moderate to severe primary restless legs syndrome, including subgroups with especially high baseline IRLS scores
edges.mechanism: Ropinirole stimulates D2 and D3 dopamine receptors, reducing the sensory-motor urge to move and lowering overall restless-legs symptom burden.
edges.summary: This is a strong protective edge for symptom severity in restless legs syndrome. The effect is consistent across short-term and longer-term placebo-controlled trials and is clinically visible on the IRLS scale.
edges.caveats: Most placebo-controlled evidence is older than the rest of Track 9 and predates more recent concerns about augmentation and impulse-control adverse effects with chronic dopamine agonist exposure. Benefit is real, but longer-term tradeoffs matter.

evidence.citation: BoganRK et al 2006 Mayo Clin Proc
evidence.notes: Ropinirole in the treatment of patients with restless legs syndrome: a US-based randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.

effect_quant.comparator: International Restless Legs Scale change with ropinirole versus placebo at 12 weeks

evidence.notes: Ropinirole is effective in the treatment of restless legs syndrome. TREAT RLS 2: a 12-week, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled study.

effect_quant.comparator: International Restless Legs Scale change with ropinirole versus placebo at 12 weeks

evidence.notes: Ropinirole in patients with restless legs syndrome and baseline IRLS total scores >= 24: efficacy and tolerability in a 26-week, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled study followed by a 40-week open-label extension.

effect_quant.comparator: International Restless Legs Scale change with ropinirole versus placebo at week 26 in patients with baseline IRLS >= 24
